title: De Novo Biosynthesis of Fatty Acids
objectives: Understand the enzymatic steps of palmitate synthesis from acetyl-CoA
Explain the role of acetyl-CoA carboxylase as the committed step
Describe the multifunctional fatty acid synthase complex
Identify regulatory mechanisms controlling fatty acid biosynthesis

overview.title: Pathway Overview
overview.content:
Fatty Acid Biosynthesis

Endergonic pathway synthesizing palmitate (16:0) from acetyl-CoA in the cytosol, primarily in liver, adipose tissue, and lactating mammary glands.

Key Features

  • Location: Cytosol (vs mitochondrial β-oxidation)
  • Main product: Palmitate (16-carbon saturated FA)
  • Energy requirements: 1 ATP + 14 NADPH per palmitate
  • Carbon source: Glucose-derived acetyl-CoA

enzymes.title: Core Enzymes
enzymes.content:
Enzyme Machinery

1. Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase (ACC)

Function: Committed step - converts acetyl-CoA → malonyl-CoA

Cofactors: Biotin, ATP, Mn2+

Domains: Biotin carboxylase + carboxyl carrier + transferase

2. Fatty Acid Synthase (FAS)

Structure: Homodimer with 7 domains per subunit

Key Domains: ACP (pantotheine), β-ketoacyl synthase (KS), enoyl reductase (ER)

Product: Palmitate after 7 elongation cycles

steps.title: Reaction Steps
steps.content:
Synthesis Mechanism

1. Substrate Provision

Acetyl-CoA: Mitochondrial export via citrate shuttle

Malonyl-CoA: ACC carboxylation (irreversible)

2. FAS Loading

MAT Domain

Action: Transfers acetyl/malonyl to ACP-Cys-SH

3-6. Elongation Cycle

KS-KR-DH-ER Domains

Steps: Condensation → Reduction → Dehydration → Reduction

Cofactors: 2 NADPH per cycle

7. Termination

Thioesterase (TE) releases palmitate (16:0)

regulation.title: Regulation
regulation.content:
Control Mechanisms

Allosteric

Activators: Citrate (indicates abundant acetyl-CoA)

Inhibitors: Palmitoyl-CoA, LCFAs (end-product feedback)

Covalent

Inactivation: AMPK phosphorylation (glucagon/epinephrine)

Activation: Insulin-stimulated dephosphorylation

Coordination

Citrate inhibits PFK-1 (glycolysis) while activating ACC

LCFAs inhibit citrate transporter & G6PD (PPP)

nadph.title: NADPH Sources
nadph.content:
Reducing Equivalents

1. Pentose Phosphate Pathway

Contribution: 50% of NADPH

Link: G6PD upregulated during lipogenesis

2. Malic Enzyme

Reaction: Malate → Pyruvate + CO2 + NADPH

Isoforms: Cytosolic (NADP-linked)

3. Isocitrate Dehydrogenase

Reaction: Isocitrate → α-KG + CO2 + NADPH

elongation.title: Post-Palmitate Modifications
elongation.content:
Elongation & Desaturation

sER Elongase System

Mechanism: Malonyl-CoA adds 2-carbon units (up to 24C)

Example: Palmitate (16:0) → Stearate (18:0)

Desaturases

Requirements: O2, NADPH, cytochrome b5

Products: Palmitoleate (16:1Δ9), Oleate (18:1Δ9)

Limitation: Cannot introduce double bonds beyond Δ9

clinical.title: Clinical Relevance
clinical.content:
Metabolic Links

Type I Diabetes

Effect: Absent insulin → ACC inactivation → reduced lipogenesis

Consequence: Elevated plasma FAs due to unrestrained lipolysis

Obesity

Pathology: Chronic insulin excess → upregulated ACC/FAS

Outcome: Excessive TAG storage in adipocytes

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Why can't humans synthesize omega-3/6 FAs?
Lack Δ12/Δ15 desaturases - must obtain linoleic (18:2Δ9,12) and α-linolenic (18:3Δ9,12,15) from diet.
How does citrate coordinate glycolysis/lipogenesis?
High citrate inhibits PFK-1 (slowing glycolysis) while activating ACC (promoting FA synthesis) when acetyl-CoA is abundant.
Why are NADPH sources compartmentalized?
PPP provides cytosolic NADPH for lipogenesis, while mitochondrial NADPH is used for antioxidant defense (glutathione system).
